Classify a pedon under the New Zealand Soil Classification

Source: R/key-nzsc4.R
classify_nzsc4.Rd

Keys a PedonRecord through the New Zealand Soil Classification, 4th edition (Manaaki Whenua - Landcare Research 2026), following its Key to Soil Orders and keys to groups and subgroups. Experimental: this release keys the 15 orders (Organic, Gley, Ultic, Podzol, Allophanic, Pumice, Melanic, Semiarid, Oxidic, Granular, Pallic, Brown, Anthropic, Recent, Raw Soils), their 77 groups (since 0.9.298, e.g. Orthic Brown Soils, Perch-gley Pallic Soils) and their 336 subgroups (keyed from 0.9.299 to 0.9.302, e.g. Peaty Orthic Gley Soils, Humose Orthic Podzol Soils, Mottled Fragic Pallic Soils, Typic Orthic Brown Soils); seven groups have no subgroups and keep the group name. The Cryic Soils of the appendix are not keyed.

Usage

classify_nzsc4(
  pedon,
  rules = NULL,
  on_missing = c("warn", "silent", "error"),
  gapfill = FALSE
)

Arguments

pedon

A PedonRecord.

rules

Optional pre-loaded rule set (load_rules("nzsc4")).

on_missing

One of "warn" (default), "silent", "error".

gapfill

Opt-in within-pedon gap-fill, as in classify_usda.

Value

A ClassificationResult with system_id "nzsc4", the deepest class in name (the subgroup, or the group where no subgroup is keyed yet), the order in rsg_or_order, the classes of each level in levels, the key trace, and provisional_because (classes before the assigned one that could not be decided).

Details

The NZSC reads horizon notations and field tests. The diagnostics read the New Zealand notation (Ah, E, Bw, Bt, Bg, Bh, Bs, Bo, Bx, Bw(g), Bhm, Bsm, Blm, CR, R, Of, Om, Oh, Lm, Lh, an e prefix for anthropic soil material; FAO designations are read by the same letters), moist Munsell colours, texture (field_texture words or codes, or lab clay, silt and sand), pH, P retention (phosphate_retention_pct), dry bulk density, volcanic glass, coarse fragments and their origin, structure, clay coatings, carbonate, ESP, and the field tests naf_test (reactive-aluminium test: none, slight, moderate, strong), childs_test, sensitivity_class, fluidity_class, stickiness and strength_moist. From the site it reads drainage_class, parent_material (Melanic Soils), anthropic_truncation and overthickened_a (the note to the key on overthickened A horizons), and designation_system. The groups also read the packing (packing_degree), Ksat (ksat_mm_h), penetration resistance, where the redox segregations are (redox_segregations_location), sulfate S, roots, a Maori cultural layer (maori_cultural_layer) and the colour of coatings; and, on the site, soil_temp_30cm_C, mean_annual_air_temp_C, surface_water, methane_odour, mechanical_mixing_depth_cm and artificially_drained. The subgroups also read sulfidic S (sulfidic_s_pct), the EC of a 1:5 extract (ec_1to5_dS_m), the share of Sphagnum in the fibres (sphagnum_fibres_pct), a shelly layer (shelly_layer), exchangeable Ca and Mg, clay films, the colour of coatings on pores (pore_coatings_hue_moist, pore_coatings_value_moist, pore_coatings_chroma_moist), the weathering of rock fragments (weathering_stage, weathered_fragments_pct) and the cementation class; on the site, mechanical_mixing_purpose and acid_neutralising_amendment (Mixed and Fill Anthropic Soils). Features a describer records when met (stratification, nodules, cracks, refuse or cultural layers, permafrost, surface water) are absent when not recorded. The choices where the text is silent are listed in system.file("rules", "nzsc4", "readings.yaml", package = "soilKey").

References

Manaaki Whenua - Landcare Research (2026). New Zealand Soil Classification. 4th ed. doi:10.7931/dl1-lrss-4-2026 .

See also

make_nzsc4_example, soilkey_systems.

Examples

res <- classify_nzsc4(make_nzsc4_example("brown"), on_missing = "silent")
res$name
#> [1] "Typic Orthic Brown Soils"
